plugins.name: attention-workflow
plugins.description: EXPERIMENTAL, Claude-only. An attention-regulating development lifecycle — Frame, Design, Prepare, authorize, Implement, Verify, Deliver, Close — carried by one orchestration skill over local run state. Versioned grants are create-only and supersede rather than rewrite; an independent verifier derives the actual route itself and its verdict stays withheld until the operator commits a judgment; narrow PreToolUse guards deny grant rewrites and unauthorized pushes. Supersedes spec-flow while enabled.

plugins.name: coach
plugins.description: ADHD-friendly productivity coaching: daily planning (/today, /energy), end-of-day capture (/checkin), weekly scheduling (/plan-week) and review (/weekly), life-direction reviews (/review), goal-to-project alignment (/align), project lifecycle (/intake, /breakdown, /reentry, /sunset), idea capture (/spark), brain dump (/dump), task triage (/triage), decision journaling (/decide), and pattern analysis (momentum, overdue-rescue) with adaptive tone calibration

plugins.name: commit
plugins.description: Format-aware atomic commits for git and jj (Jujutsu). One skill covering commit, split, message review, and retrofitting edits into earlier commits (jj absorb / git fixup). Auto-detects VCS and commit message style from repo context. Includes PreToolUse hook that blocks destructive working-copy operations.

plugins.name: compass
plugins.description: A suite of conversational thinking tools — reflect (Socratic mirror, never recommends, always saves), mull (thinking partner, probes AND contributes opinions, saves substantive sessions only), and converge (advisor, leads with a researched recommendation plus confidence % and refines it one question at a time). Plus a paired evaluation track: first-principles (evidence-first interview that produces a signed-off needs map before any option is named) hands off to solution-research (turns that map into a systems-first parallel-research handoff prompt).

plugins.name: craft
plugins.description: Software craftsmanship discipline skills: grill (the interview primitive — walk a design tree one question at a time, facts looked up by subagent rather than asked, no acting until shared understanding), grill-with-docs (that loop applied to vocabulary, against per-repo CONTEXT.md glossaries), diagnose, prototype, tdd, improve-codebase-architecture, grok (stateful multi-session codebase comprehension with supersession-aware understanding records), zoom-out (adapted in part from mattpocock/skills, MIT), infra-review (architecture/security review of Terraform+Atlantis PRs), quiz-me (opt-in active-recall comprehension check after a code explanation), interrogate-model (holistic representability review of a domain model — the legitimate scenarios and personas it cannot express), design-by-stories (design an artifact's shape — schema, template, data model, config — by modeling its actors and user stories first, then deriving the shape from the stories), and lucid-architecture-diagram (drive AWS cloud architecture diagrams in Lucid, including the two silent-failure modes of its API). derive-conventions (derive a repo's unwritten house style from its own code, adjudicate each inferred rule with the human, and write the approved set to CONVENTIONS.md so the review agents stop re-deriving it). wizard (author an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through the steps only they can perform — third-party dashboards, credentials, CI secrets, one-off cutovers — from a hardened template), resolve-conflicts (recover each side's intent from commits, PRs, tickets and NDR heads before resolving a merge, rebase, or jj conflict; detects git vs jj and follows that VCS's own mechanics), and wait-what (user-invoked: re-pitch a message that did not land, in Simplified Technical English using the repo's own vocabulary) — all three adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT. Three read-only post-edit review agents ride along, each deriving the host repository's conventions rather than importing preferences: house-style-reviewer (a diff against the repo's own unlinted conventions, skipping whatever its linters already enforce), comment-reviewer (docstrings against the code they describe, including comments left unchanged while the code beneath them moved), and copy-reviewer (user-facing strings against the voice the product already uses). Composes with spec-flow and ndr plugins.

plugins.name: debate
plugins.description: Dialectical decision analysis: dispatch parallel advocate agents to research opposing perspectives, optionally fact-check claims, challenge the consensus with devil's advocacy, and independently synthesize a verdict. Three modes (Quick/Standard/Deep) control pipeline depth. Not for factual lookups or simple preferences.

plugins.name: feedback
plugins.description: A two-sided loop for improving agent plugins from test sessions. The 'session' skill (tester side) turns the current session record into a copy-pasteable report grading the plugins exercised; the 'triage' skill (author side) aggregates many reports into a prioritized action plan, routing each finding to a concrete fix. Both share one report-format contract.

plugins.name: introspect
plugins.description: Introspection tooling for Claude Code itself. usage-report: reconstruct how a person works with Claude Code in a repo (skills, slash commands, subagents, MCP tools, task-kickoff style, activity over time) from their local session transcripts, via a stdlib-only read-only parser. conversation-temperature: read the local user's own authored register across all their transcripts — terseness, heat, and warmth, led by marker rates and real quoted messages rather than composite indices. Both run locally against the user's own transcripts and make no network calls; usage-report emits names and counts only, while conversation-temperature quotes the user's own messages back to them by design.

plugins.name: langfuse
plugins.description: Sends Claude Code and Codex session traces to Langfuse via a Stop hook — per-turn traces with prompts, generations, tool observations, and backdated timestamps. Includes a SessionStart tripwire that marks programmatically-spawned sessions.

LANGFUSE_BASE_URL.description: Langfuse host. Use https://us.cloud.langfuse.com for US, https://cloud.langfuse.com for EU, or your self-hosted URL.

plugins.name: librarian
plugins.description: Curates, catalogs, retrieves, and maintains your library of notes and knowledge in an Obsidian vault. Workflow-shaped (Capture / Process / Retrieve / Maintain) and agent-mediated (skills draft, agents execute). 19 skills + 4 agents + 6 references, coupled to the vault conventions in ~/Loose Ends/.claude/rules/{wiki.md,catalog.md} and the Templater templates in ~/Loose Ends/Templates/.

word_log.title: Word log
word_log.description: Vault-relative path of the note /term appends to on this machine

plugins.name: linear
plugins.description: Linear workflow conventions for a small two-person team. Owns ticket creation defaults (including assignee), status flow semantics, label set, title shape, collaboration conventions, and MCP call patterns. Composes with spec-flow (which uses Linear as a contract host but defers to this plugin for the conventions). Includes a doctor skill for workspace setup validation, and a linear-ops agent that executes decided ticket writes in isolated context — resolving identifiers, applying the MCP silent-failure workarounds, and verifying what landed.

plugins.name: pm
plugins.description: PM helpers for team Linear workflows. Skills for single-ticket authoring (a short shaping interview, body composed to the shared issue-body spec), the weekly grooming loop (per-person WIP), plan-to-tickets breakdown (assignee-aware), chart-first mapping of efforts too large to plan in one session, questionnaires that pull a blocking decision out of someone else's head, and end-of-cycle retro notes (attribution + Linear-first output). Composes with the linear plugin; ndr and librarian integrations are optional externals.

plugins.name: shake-tune
plugins.description: Interpret Klippain Shake Tune results for 3D printers: diagnose issues from PNG graphs, explain findings, recommend fixes, and track results over time. Supports belt comparison, input shaper, vibration profile, axes map, and excitation tests.

plugins.name: skillsmith
plugins.description: Craft and upkeep of skills. Authoring reference (the vocabulary and principles that make any agent-consumed document predictable — a skill, an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, a rules file, a doc reached by a pointer) plus provenance tracking for borrowed work: compares an adapted skill to its pinned upstream, flags behavioral drift and fabricated attributions, and refreshes the reviewed commit SHA. Houses writing-for-agents and upstream-review.

plugins.name: spec-flow
plugins.description: Personal SDLC scaffolding for AI-assisted development. A lightweight, ephemeral 'contract' between user and AI drives each code change from captured idea to verified done; the durable layer (CLAUDE.md, ndr atoms, README) lives elsewhere. Lifecycle: capture -> draft -> implement -> close.

plugins.name: teach
plugins.description: A stateful, multi-session teaching workspace routed into the Obsidian vault. The /teach skill grounds learning in the user's documented learning style and high-trust sources, builds a mission, resources, glossary, and learning records as vault notes under the topic's best-fit context, and writes lessons as markdown notes that transclude the wiki's prose and add a pure-CSS self-grading quiz (via a shipped snippet, no plugin or JS). Cheat sheets and reference material live as ordinary wiki pages, not HTML. Entry altitude is set by question altitude and graph density, with learning records as the only gate on mastery claims. Grounds in owned textbooks via DEVONthink when available and pins live-code citations to immutable refs. Requires an Obsidian vault (obsidian-cli); optionally surfaces owned textbooks from DEVONthink. Adapted from mattpocock/skills (MIT, © 2026 Matt Pocock).

plugins.name: teardown
plugins.description: Study foreign open-source projects to extract transferable architectural lessons into the Obsidian vault. `/teardown` runs a study session over a local clone, or over files fetched at a pinned SHA when no clone exists, dispatching a read-only `surveyor` agent per project through two ordered phases (current structure, then history/rationale) descending one user-picked layer at a time (system map, domain model, code), spot-checking citations before any write, and adding each layer to an interactive Artifact page and to one of two note types: a single-concern QUESTION note that accretes comparison rows across projects over time, or a whole-system PROJECT note anchored on a mental model. Both carry `projects_surveyed:` frontmatter pinning the repo, commit SHA, and date read — the index and the read log in one place. `/teardown-recheck` audits that pin against the corpus's current HEAD, diffing cited files since the recorded SHA and verifying that cited line numbers still point at what the note claims, so drift is caught instead of trusted. A reference instrument for lookup, not a learning exercise. Composes with librarian (graduation, refresh) and ndr (decisions about the user's own projects); distinct from craft:grok, which studies repos the user owns and intends to change.

plugins.name: workspaces
plugins.description: Teaches agents that isolated per-agent checkouts exist in jj-colocated repos via `jjx` (jj's equivalent of a git worktree), and how to drive it: `jjx open <slug>` creates or idempotently resumes a managed sibling workspace and prints its path on stdout, `--from <revset>` bases it on an explicit revision instead of the caller's uncommitted state, `jjx open --unique <slug>` forces a fresh workspace for fan-out, `jjx add <path>` adds an existing checkout at an explicit path, and `jjx rm <path>` cleans up without discarding unsaved work. The single skill exists to be found by the failure it prevents — an agent about to conclude that parallel isolated work isn't possible in a jj repo, or reaching for a plain git worktree instead.
